topic_1_procedural_memory.topic: Procedural memory in LLM agents — the gap between factual/experiential/working memory and procedural 'how-to' knowledge

key_papers.title: ProcMEM: Learning Reusable Procedural Memory from Experience via Non-Parametric PPO for LLM Agents
key_papers.main_claim: Proposes ProcMEM, a framework that autonomously learns reusable procedural 'Skills' from interaction experience without parameter updates. Formalizes a Skill-MDP with activation/execution/termination conditions and uses Non-Parametric PPO (semantic gradients + PPO Gate trust-region verification) to evolve high-quality skills.
key_papers.how_it_works: 1) Skill-MDP formalization: Skills are tuples ⟨I_ω, π_ω, β_ω⟩ with natural-language activation, execution procedures, and termination conditions. 2) Non-Parametric PPO: Semantic gradients extracted from batch trajectories via hindsight attribution propose skill refinements; a PPO Gate computes clipped surrogate advantage to verify candidates before acceptance. 3) Score-based maintenance: Online advantage-style scoring prunes low-utility skills to maintain compact pool.

key_papers.title: LEGOMem: Modular Procedural Memory for Multi-agent LLM Systems for Workflow Automation
key_papers.main_claim: Introduces LEGOMem, a modular procedural memory framework for multi-agent LLM systems that decomposes past task trajectories into reusable memory units (full-task memories and subtask memories) flexibly allocated across orchestrators and task agents.
key_papers.how_it_works: 1) Memory distillation: Successful executions distilled into structured memory units (full-task plans + subtask behaviors). 2) Memory bank indexed by semantic embeddings. 3) Three retrieval strategies: vanilla, dynamic retrieval, query rewriting. 4) During new tasks, orchestrator gets full-task memories for planning/delegation; task agents get subtask memories aligned with delegated subtasks.

numerical_results.officebench_improvements: All LEGOMem variants significantly improve task success rates over memory-less and baseline methods
key_findings: Orchestrator memory is critical for high-level planning and delegation
Fine-grained subtask retrieval provides meaningful gains for smaller agents
Teams of smaller models with memory narrow gap with stronger agents

key_papers.title: ReMe: Remember Me, Refine Me — A Dynamic Procedural Memory Framework for Experience-Driven Agent Evolution
key_papers.main_claim: Proposes ReMe, a dynamic procedural memory framework that shifts from passive accumulation to feedback-driven evolution via three mechanisms: multi-faceted distillation (success patterns, failure triggers, comparative insights), context-adaptive reuse (scenario-aware indexing, reranking, adaptive rewriting), and utility-based refinement (autonomous addition/pruning based on reuse utility).
key_papers.how_it_works: 1) Multi-faceted distillation extracts fine-grained experiences from trajectories. 2) Context-adaptive reuse tailors historical insights to new contexts via scenario-aware indexing, reranking, and adaptive rewriting. 3) Utility-based refinement tracks utility of each experience during reuse, periodically pruning low-utility entries.

numerical_results.appworld: Establishes new state-of-the-art in agent memory systems
numerical_results.key_insight: Memory quality can substitute for model scale: Qwen3-8B + ReMe > Qwen3-14B without memory

topic_2_schema_agnostic_kg_shacl.topic: Schema-agnostic knowledge graph construction with SHACL validation

key_papers.title: ANCHOR: Schema-Agnostic Knowledge Graph Construction via Hybrid Ontology Discovery for Cyber Threat Intelligence
key_papers.main_claim: Presents ANCHOR, a schema-agnostic CTI knowledge graph construction system that bridges LLMs and formal ontology schemas via hybrid ontology discovery (embedding search + LLM-guided recursive navigation) combined with SHACL-based validation for schema-compliant type assignments.
key_papers.how_it_works: 1) Schema-agnostic extraction: Preprocesses CTI docs, extracts entities/coreferences/triplets without binding to fixed schema. 2) Hybrid ontology discovery: Embedding-based search (score = 0.5*sim(query, class_name) + 0.5*sim(query, class_desc) + keyword bonus) with threshold τ_entity=0.45, τ_predicate=0.30; falls back to hierarchical recursive navigation. 3) SHACL validation with closed-loop self-correction: Violations trigger LLM-based self-correction (max 3 attempts). 4) MCP-compatible tool interface for ontology exploration.

numerical_results.local_llm_performance: Retains 99.2% (entity) and 97.8% (predicate) of best enterprise LLM performance

key_papers.title: Evidence-Carrying Validation for Knowledge Graphs
key_papers.main_claim: Proposes evidence-carrying validation for SHACL: every selected node–shape check returns a satisfaction trace (pass) or failure witness (fail), mutually recursive through negation, preserving constraint structure, cardinality evidence, and concrete graph support.
key_papers.how_it_works: 1) Shared shape algebra formalizes constraints. 2) Satisfaction traces and failure witnesses ground each verdict in constraints, cardinality decisions, and supporting triples. 3) Implemented in Shifty (Python), preserves authored identities through normalization, exposes typed result objects. 4) Enables consumers to explain results, extract conforming data, diagnose target selection, propose repairs without re-invoking validator.

numerical_results.practical_impact: Overhead matters less once validation completes in milliseconds, enabling evidence in every iteration of authoring/agent loop
numerical_results.case_study: Passing and failing evidence together locate missing metadata and select domain-consistent repair

key_papers.title: Rewrite Once, Validate Anywhere: Producing OWL-Aware SHACL Constraints (ShacOWL)
key_papers.main_claim: Introduces ShacOWL, a tool that rewrites SHACL shapes based on OWL ontologies (OWL EL⁻ fragment) to enable ontology-aware validation without requiring OWL reasoning at validation time. Data-independent rewriting produces new shapes graph applicable to any data graph with any SHACL validator.
key_papers.how_it_works: 1) Identifies OWL EL⁻ fragment (supports nominals, role chains, qualified existential restrictions on LHS) avoiding exponential blow-ups. 2) Rewrites targets and constraints based on ontology axioms (subclass, subproperty). 3) Single SHACL validator needed for varying data graphs with fixed ontology/shapes. 4) Benchmarked against reasoner-then-validate approach.

numerical_results.validation_times: Pure validation times similar between rewrite-then-validate vs reason-then-validate approaches
numerical_results.implementation: Java OWL API wrappers, available at github.com/gorczyca/owl-aware-shacl

topic_3_experiential_reflective_learning.topic: Experiential Reflective Learning (ERL) for self-improving agents

key_papers.title: Experiential Reflective Learning for Self-Improving LLM Agents
key_papers.main_claim: Introduces Experiential Reflective Learning (ERL), a self-improvement framework where agents reflect on task trajectories and outcomes to generate reusable heuristics. At test time, relevant heuristics are retrieved and injected into context. On Gaia2 benchmark, ERL improves success rate by +7.8% over ReAct baseline, outperforms ExpeL and AutoGuide, and works from single-attempt trajectories without retries.
key_papers.how_it_works: 1) Heuristic generation: After each task, agent reflects on trajectory + outcome to generate structured heuristic with (a) analysis of success/failure cause, (b) learned guideline with trigger conditions and recommended actions. 2) Retrieval-augmented execution: For new tasks, LLM scores stored heuristics for relevance (similarity, diversity, informativeness), top-k (k=20) injected into system prompt. 3) Single-attempt extraction: No multiple rollouts or contrastive pairs needed.

key_findings: Selective retrieval is essential (no retrieval drops to 53.8%)
Heuristics provide more transferable abstractions than few-shot trajectory prompting
Failure heuristics excel on Search (+14.3%), success heuristics on Execution (+9.0%)
Single-attempt experience sufficient — no retries needed

topic_4_ontology_grounding_hallucination.topic: Ontology grounding as hallucination mitigation — ontology-constrained decoding and schema-enforced generation

key_papers.title: Ontology-Constrained Generation of Domain-Specific Clinical Summaries
key_papers.main_claim: Proposes ontology-guided constrained decoding to reduce hallucinations while improving relevance in clinical summarization. Leverages medical ontologies to create domain-adapted summaries (structured and unstructured). Evaluation on MIMIC-III shows improvements in domain-adapted summaries and hallucination reduction.
key_papers.how_it_works: 1) Ontology-guided constrained decoding: Ontology constraints applied during decoding to ensure generated content adheres to domain schema. 2) Domain-adapted summaries: Different specialties (oncology, radiology, etc.) get tailored summaries based on relevant ontology concepts. 3) Structured + unstructured output: Generates both structured (ontology-aligned) and unstructured summaries.

numerical_results.results: Demonstrates improvements in generating domain-adapted summaries and hallucination reduction (specific metrics not extracted from abstract)

key_papers.title: To Know is to Construct: Schema-Constrained Generation for Agent Memory (SCG-MEM)
key_papers.main_claim: Proposes SCG-MEM, a schema-constrained generative memory architecture that reformulates memory access as Schema-Constrained Generation. Maintains a dynamic Cognitive Schema (Prefix Trie) that strictly constrains LLM decoding to generate only valid memory entry keys, providing formal guarantee against structural hallucinations. Models memory updates via Piagetian assimilation (grounding into existing schema) and accommodation (schema expansion).
key_papers.how_it_works: 1) Cognitive Schema as Prefix Trie: Discrete concepts form the agent's epistemic boundary. 2) Schema-constrained decoding: During recollection, Trie functions as hard constraint on LLM decoding — any token resulting in prefix outside schema receives zero probability. 3) Assimilation/Accommodation: New inputs either ground into existing schema (assimilation) or expand schema with novel concepts (accommodation). 4) Associative Graph: Enables multi-hop reasoning via activation propagation over schema.

numerical_results.locoMo_benchmark: Substantially improves performance across all categories over retrieval-based baselines
numerical_results.structural_hallucination_elimination: Formal guarantee: agent mathematically incapable of generating key k̂ ∉ S
numerical_results.key_metrics: Outperforms dense retrieval (semantic gap) and unconstrained generative memory (structural hallucination)

key_papers.title: Scientific Knowledge-driven Decoding Constraints Improving the Reliability of LLMs (SciDC)
key_papers.main_claim: Proposes SciDC, a multi-layered constraint framework that converts flexible scientific knowledge into standardized decoding constraints. Three-layer constraints: top-layer (macro-structure/reasoning steps), middle-layer (conditional logic with local regeneration), bottom-layer (token-level logit masking for syntactic/numerical feasibility). Uses strong GLLM as knowledge compiler and local DLLM for constrained generation.
key_papers.how_it_works: 1) GLLM parses domain knowledge into three-layer rule set R_T (top), R_M (middle), R_B (bottom). 2) DLLM performs generation with constraints integrated at each decoding stage. 3) Top-layer: Enforces step-by-step reasoning sequence via prompt design. 4) Middle-layer: Conditional validation loops with dynamic option selection for multi-hop dependency checks and local regeneration. 5) Bottom-layer: Direct logit masking and regex-based generation for numerical/categorical feasibility.

numerical_results.average_accuracy_improvement: 12% over vanilla generation across scientific tasks
numerical_results.architecture: GLLM (knowledge compiler) + DLLM (constrained generation) collaborative framework

topic_5_runtime_ontology_evolution.topic: Runtime ontology evolution and dynamic ontologies for autonomous systems

key_papers.title: Evo-DKD: Dual-Knowledge Decoding for Autonomous Ontology Evolution in Large Language Models
key_papers.main_claim: Proposes Evo-DKD, a dual-decoder framework for autonomous ontology evolution combining structured ontology traversal with unstructured text reasoning. Two parallel decoding streams: structured decoder generates candidate ontology edits (new concepts/relations), unstructured decoder produces natural-language justifications. Dynamic attention-based gating coordinates streams. Closed reasoning loop: proposed edits validated (consistency checks + cross-verification) then injected into KB, informing subsequent reasoning.
key_papers.how_it_works: 1) Dual-decoder architecture: Structured Decoder (ontology stream) generates triples/axioms; Unstructured Decoder (text stream) generates explanations. 2) Dynamic gating: Attention-based gating computes α_t ∈ [0,1] balancing structured vs unstructured output at each step (switching mode or mixture mode). 3) Validation module: Checks ontology consistency/constraints + justification cross-check via LLM verification. 4) Closed-loop: Validated edits inserted into KB, fed back as context for next iteration.

key_results.healthcare_relaxed_match: Full Dual-Decoder and Structured-only both achieve 0.7+
key_results.cultural_heritage: Full Dual-Decoder shows clear improvement over Structured-only
key_results.semantic_search: Most difficult domain, low relaxed match across all modes
key_results.bertscore: Full Dual-Decoder substantially outperforms other modes across all domains

numerical_results.case_study: Ozempic triple (Ozempic, manages, weight) added to healthcare KG; RAG query 'What drugs for weight loss in diabetes?' goes from no answer to correct identification after update

key_papers.title: A Methodological Framework for Runtime Ontology Evolution in Dynamic Environments
key_papers.main_claim: Proposes a methodological and architectural framework for runtime update of ontologies and knowledge bases, enabling intelligent systems to autonomously adapt their internal world representation during execution. Distinguishes between previously unknown concepts and known concepts enriched with new instances, integrating information in a controlled, consistent manner.
key_papers.how_it_works: 1) Perception Layer: Visual perception + semantic interpretation via LLMs. 2) Semantic Interpretation Layer: Generates candidate triplets from observations. 3) Ontology and KB Management Layer: Distinguishes conceptual vs instance-level updates; generates valid OWL constructs; manages inverse properties, datatype normalization; prevents semantic degradation. 4) Reasoning and Decision Support Layer: Exploits updated ontology for reasoning/decision-making. 5) Validation: Laboratory scenarios demonstrating knowledge gap recognition, differentiated updates, controlled integration.

numerical_results.validation_approach: Qualitative validation in laboratory dynamic scenarios (MUSIC4D and MHARA projects)
scenarios_tested: Instance population: New musical instrument recognized as instance of known concept — KB populated, schema unchanged
Conceptual schema evolution: New concept types added with formal validation
Consistency preservation: OWL construct generation, inverse property management, datatype normalization
numerical_results.key_contribution: End-to-end pipeline combining perception, LLM interpretation, and robust ontology update mechanism with formal consistency guarantees

key_papers.title: Liquid Interfaces: A Dynamic Ontology for the Interoperability of Autonomous Systems
key_papers.main_claim: Introduces Liquid Interfaces, a coordination paradigm where interfaces are ephemeral relational events emerging through intention articulation and semantic negotiation at runtime, not persistent technical artifacts. Formalizes Liquid Interface Protocol (LIP) governing intention-driven interaction, negotiated execution, and enforced ephemerality under semantic uncertainty.
key_papers.how_it_works: 1) Intentional Primacy: Interaction validity determined by semantic alignment with declared intention (entropy reduction), not syntactic compliance. 2) Mandatory Temporal Dissolution: All negotiated schemas/bindings invalidated upon completion — zero residual coupling. 3) Negotiation Function: Iteratively synthesizes provisional protocol minimizing semantic entropy until confidence exceeds threshold. 4) Bounded Liquidity: Entropy threshold defines boundary; fallback modes (recursive simplification, solidification to core ontology) when negotiation fails. 5) Intention-Based Access Control (IBAC): Governance evaluated against intent, not endpoints.

formal_invariants: Invariant I: Intentional Primacy — ΔH(shared_semantic_state) < 0 required
Invariant II: Mandatory Temporal Dissolution — ∀t_complete: interface_artifacts(t) = ∅
Invariant III: Bounded Residual Coupling — residual_coupling → 0 across episodes
Invariant IV: Composable Intent Resolution — multi-agent capability composition
numerical_results.negotiation_convergence: Iterative until semantic confidence > safety threshold θ; max steps bounded
numerical_results.fallback_modes: 1) Recursive Simplification 2) Solidification to pre-agreed core ontology
